issue.title: Open PDFs stay in step with bob (Highlights saves first, then reloads in place)
issue.description: When `bob ref scan` or `bob ref sync -w` on the Mac updates a ref PDF's page-1 marker, it never again strands an open Highlights document. bob writes through a bounded macOS file-coordination write (`NSFileCoordinator`, `.forMerging`). macOS has Highlights save your unsaved annotations first, bob re-checks the marker in the fresh bytes and writes, and Highlights reloads the same tab in place: no dialog, no keystroke, no tab change. Anything uncertain becomes a hold: nothing is written for that PDF, and the next scan retries. That covers you actively reading in Highlights, Highlights not answering, and the marker changing under bob. CLI and JSON always report what happened. Bob Mac Capture posts one quiet, grouped notification, only when a PDF that is open in Highlights was refreshed or Highlights needs you. The feature ships behind `highlights.coordinate_pdf_writes` and is enabled after a guided real-Highlights acceptance test.

issue.title: macOS file-coordination primitive
issue.description: coordinate: add `native::file_coordination`, a bounded `.forMerging` coordinated write. On macOS it is `NSFileCoordinator` through objc2, objc2-foundation, and block2 (macOS-only dependencies), with a watchdog that calls `cancel()` when the budget expires and returns Granted/Held/Failed truthfully. Elsewhere it runs the closure directly. Add a macOS-only test that compiles a small Swift NSDocument presenter fixture with `swiftc` and proves three cases: no presenter writes; a dirty presenter saves first and reloads clean; a blocked presenter is held within the budget with no write. Nothing calls the primitive yet.

issue.title: Coordination config, reading-activity probe, and budgets
issue.description: policy: parse `highlights.coordinate_pdf_writes` (bool, default false) into `HighlightsConfig`. Add a reading-activity probe: on macOS, `lsappinfo` for the frontmost bundle id (any `net.highlightsapp.*`) and `ioreg` `HIDIdleTime`, each bounded at 2 s; elsewhere it always reports not reading. The output parsers are pure and unit-tested, a probe failure reports unknown, and internal env overrides exist for tests. Add the budget constants: 10 s per PDF, a 30 s scan cap, and a 30 s reading window, each with an internal env override. Bundle these into one `PdfWritePolicy` value, built once per command. issue.title: Coordinated marker writes, holds, and human reporting
issue.description: executor: when the policy is on, wrap each marker-write PDF's whole v1/v2 write sequence in one coordinated accessor. That covers scan (human and JSON), `ref sync -w`, and create-time ingest. Inside the accessor, re-check the PDF first. Same digest: write as today. Changed digest with the same marker: write to the freshly located annotation and record saved-first. Changed marker: hold `marker_changed`. Add the `editor_active` reading hold for unattended scans only, plus the new `-a, --attended` scan flag, and the `coordination_timeout` hold with the per-PDF budget and scan cap. Add `ScanWriteOutcome::Held` and the marker-write report (mode, saved-first, status transition, wait time). Holds exit 0. Add the yellow `held` concise line, the summary count, and the verbose and `ref sync` lines. JSON mode counts holds as neither notes nor failures for now. With the key off, output stays byte-identical. Document the contract and the config key, then run `just docs-gen` for the flag.

issue.title: Scan JSON fields, scan receipt, and the Darwin notification
issue.description: report: add the additive scan JSON fields (schema stays 1): `summary.held`, `notes[].marker_write {mode, editor_saved_first, status{from,to}?}`, and a top-level `held[] {pdf, note, title, reason, message}` appended after `queued`. Extract one envelope builder shared by JSON and human modes. Every writing `ref scan` that acquired the scan writer lock atomically writes that exact envelope to `<state>/bob-cli/ref/last-scan.json` (0600). That includes human and JSON modes, intake-only drains, and hard failures after the lock. Then, on macOS, it calls `notify_post("org.bobs.bob.ref.scan-finished")`. A receipt failure only warns on stderr. Document the fields, receipt, and notification in highlights-ref-sync.md and the JSON reference.

issue.title: Bob Mac Capture core decoding and open-PDF presentation
issue.description: mac-core: in the linked bob-mac-capture repo, RefsCore decodes the new scan fields tolerantly. Those are `generated_at`, `summary.held`, `held[]` (lossy rows), and `notes[].marker_write`. Add a bounded receipt reader that resolves the path like bob: `XDG_STATE_HOME`, else `~/.local/state`. Add a pure `RefsPDFUpdates` classifier that takes a response plus optional open-tab file names. It splits entries into refreshed-open, refreshed-quiet, reading holds, busy holds, and changed holds, and supplies dedupe keys. Add the exact copy deck for notifications, footer clauses, and the busy banner, using the Refs state vocabulary. Unit-test it all and run `just portable-check`.

issue.title: Bob Mac Capture receipt observer, notifications, and settings
issue.description: mac-app: in bob-mac-capture, observe `org.bobs.bob.ref.scan-finished` with `notify_register_dispatch` and read the receipt off the main thread. Dedupe by content hash. Only when needed, check open tabs with the existing read-only Highlights tab reader, and never prompt for Accessibility. When the panel is hidden, post a passive, silent, threaded `refs-scan` notification that selects the row. When the panel is visible, show a footer clause or the busy banner with Scan Again. Notify for busy holds once per PDF. Add the Settings › References toggle "Tell me when Bob updates an open PDF" (on by default). ⌘S passes `-a`, with a remembered retry for an older bob. Update the refs, settings, and protocol docs, compile on the Mac where reachable, and rely on macOS CI.
